base_override.reason: SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH (title insurer consolidating annuity/life insurer F&G): the engine's OCF-based conservative OE is rejected as the base — for an insurer consolidating F&G, operating cash flow is policyholder plumbing, not distributable earnings: annuity deposits and the build in future policy benefits run through OCF while the corresponding investment deployment sits in investing (purchases of investment securities $23,198M in FY2025). FY2025 OCF was $5,828,000,000 against net income of $602,000,000, and NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE fires for 2023, 2024 and 2025; the engine's normalized OCF base is $23.6827/share — a 59.5% OE yield at $39.80 for a company whose filed diluted EPS was $2.21 in FY2025. Capitalizing that base prints a fake Tier S. For an insurer, net income is the honest owner's-earnings proxy (the ALLY/FUTU/LPLA/WSE/ARCC sector precedent in this sweep): SBC is already expensed inside it, title claim provisions and F&G benefit/reserve charges are already charged inside it, and the median-of-3-FY normalization mirrors the engine's own base method applied to that definition. The median is conservative for this name: FY2025 net income carries an abnormal tax load (income tax $753,000,000 on pre-tax $1,397,000,000, a 54% rate, including the F&G-distribution deferred-tax adjustment in Corporate & Other, which lost $458M attributable in FY2025), and GAAP NI is below adjusted net earnings in every recent year (H1 2026 adjusted EPS $2.31 vs GAAP $1.98). Declared under bounded authority (c): every input is a figure printed by this run's engine output (financials_history.csv).

description.text: The following describes the business of Fidelity National Financial, Inc. and its subsidiaries. Except where otherwise noted, all references to "we," "us," "our", the "Company" or "FNF" are to Fidelity National Financial, Inc. and its subsidiaries, taken together. We are a leading provider of (i) title insurance, escrow and other title-related services, including trust activities, trustee sales guarantees, recordings and reconveyances and home warranty and (ii) transaction services to the real estate and mortgage industries. FNF is one of the nation’s largest title insurance companies operating through its title insurance underwriters - Fidelity National Title Insurance Company ("FNTIC"), Chicago Title Insurance Company ("Chicago Title"), Commonwealth Land Title Insurance Company ("Commonwealth Land Title"), Alamo Title Insurance ("Alamo Title") and National Title Insurance of New York Inc. ("National Title of New York") - which collectively issue more title insurance policies than any other title company in the United States. Through our subsidiary ServiceLink Holdings, LLC ("ServiceLink"), we provide mortgage transaction services including title-related services and facilitation of production and management of mortgage loans. We are also a leading provider of insurance solutions serving retail annuity and life customers and institutional clients through our majority-owned subsidiary, F&G Annuities & Life, Inc. ("F&G").

about.description_short: Fidelity National Financial, Inc. (NYSE: FNF) is a leading provider of title insurance and transaction services to the real estate and mortgage industries, and a leading provider of insurance solutions serving retail annuity and life customers and institutional clients through its majority owned subsidiary F&G Annuities & Life, Inc. (NYSE: FG). FNF is the nation's largest title insurance company through its title insurance underwriters - Fidelity National Title, Chicago Title, Commonwealth Land Title, Alamo Title and National Title of New York - that collectively issue more title insurance policies than any other title company in the United States.

# FNF — Fidelity National Financial, Inc.
v5 run, 2026-10-19. All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json or financials_history.csv — none are recomputed.

## What it is
The largest U.S. title insurer (direct premiums $2,574M and agency premiums $3,250M in FY2025) plus majority-owned F&G Annuities & Life (annuities, IUL, pension risk transfer; F&G contributed 30% of FY2025 adjusted net earnings). On December 31, 2025 FNF distributed ~12% of F&G to shareholders as a special stock dividend (~$500M of value, ~16M FG shares), retaining ~70% and control. FY2025 filer-total revenue $14,445,000,000 (fundamentals.json) — Title $8,490M, F&G $5,731M, Corporate & Other $341M, eliminations -$117M. Price $39.62, market cap $10.777B — in scope under $40B.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv, override-filled):** operating cash flow $5,828,000,000; capex $147,000,000 — by override, see OVERRIDE (capex); SBC $88,000,000.
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025 (engine definition): $5.593B = $20.56/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE total $5.593B, latest FY OE/share $20.56; normalized 3-yr median $23.14/share). OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years on this definition.
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): $1,299,000,000 for FY2025 in financials_history.csv — an order of magnitude below the conservative figure, and the gap between the two definitions is the whole story of this name (see below).
- Balance sheet (latest CSV row): total assets $109,014,000,000, liabilities $100,042,000,000, equity $7,424,000,000 — the liability stack is mostly F&G policyholder obligations, not borrowings. Engine net debt $1.764B (key_numbers.md) is the LongTermDebt total tag ($4,400M) minus cash ($2,636M); holding-company cash and short-term liquid investments were $659M at year-end 2025 per the FY2025 release. Net debt / normalized OE 2.93x (key_numbers.md) mixes an industrial leverage lens with an insurer balance sheet and is not a solvency signal here.

**Why the OCF base is rejected:** consolidated OCF at an insurer consolidating an annuity writer is policyholder plumbing. Annuity deposits and the build in future policy benefits run through operating cash flow (FY2025 "Benefits & other policy reserve changes" alone were $3,963M of expense in the segment statement), while the corresponding asset deployment — purchases of investment securities of $23,198M in FY2025 — sits in investing activities, outside both OCF and the engine's capex leg. FY2025 net income was $602,000,000 against OCF of $5,828,000,000. The engine's normalized OCF base of $23.14/share is a 58.4% OE yield at the $39.62 price (dcf_numbers.json diagnostics, oe_yield on the unpinned run) for a company whose filed diluted EPS was $2.21 — a measurement artifact, not a bargain signal. On that base the same scenario set prints Tier S (see method range).

**TTM check (ttm.py, filing-direct, through Q2 2026):**
- OCF: FY $5,828,000,000 − prior YTD $3,011,000,000 + current YTD $2,746,000,000 = **TTM $5,563,000,000**
- SBC: FY $88,000,000 − prior YTD $41,000,000 + current YTD $46,000,000 = **TTM $93,000,000**
- Capex: ttm.py's legs are a period-mismatch artifact, stated plainly — with no capex fact filed since FY2014, it pulled the FY2014 figure ($210,000,000) and 2014/2015 quarterly legs and printed TTM capex of $217,000,000. That leg is not used; the filing capex is the override below (~$147M/yr).
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **268,000,000**
- **TTM OE total $5,253,000,000 → $19.6007/share** — the TTM version of the same rejected OCF definition, quoted because STALE_FY requires the check, not because it is used. TTM net income (fundamentals.json) is $772,000,000 on TTM revenue of $15,358,000,000 (+13.0% YoY).

**Base used = median of the last 3 fiscal years' net income per diluted share, $2.21/share, via base_override (bounded authority (c)):** FY2023 $517,000,000 / 271,000,000 = $1.9077; FY2024 $1,270,000,000 / 273,000,000 = $4.6520; FY2025 $602,000,000 / 272,000,000 = $2.2132; median $2.2132 (the FY2025 value; key_numbers.md rounds it to $2.21, base source: agent_supplied_ttm_override). For an insurer, net income is the honest owner's-earnings proxy (the ALLY/FUTU/LPLA/WSE/ARCC sector precedent in this sweep): SBC is already expensed inside it, and title claim provisions and F&G benefit/reserve charges are already charged inside it. Two properties of this construction matter: (1) the engine's net income is the *attributable* figure — FY2025 non-controlling interests of $77M were deducted before it (Title attributable $960M, F&G $217M, Corporate & Other -$458M, eliminations -$117M, summing to the $602M used), so the minority share of F&G is already removed and there is no LVS-style minority leak in this base; (2) the median year is a depressed one — FY2025 GAAP net income carries a $471M noncash deferred-tax charge triggered by the F&G share distribution (it dropped FNF's F&G ownership below 80%; FY2025 income tax was $753,000,000 on pre-tax earnings of $1,397,000,000, a 54% rate). The scenario starts below carry part of that normalization; the rest is the method range. One normalization was NOT made, stated with its size: the base year is the last year at the old F&G ownership — on December 31, 2025 FNF distributed ~12% of F&G (ownership ~82% → ~70%), so ≈12/82 of FY2025's $217M attributable F&G earnings (≈$32M, ≈$0.12/share) comes from a stake FNF shareholders now hold directly as FG shares (a ~$500M special stock dividend), not through FNF. Normalizing the FY2025 year to the retained stake gives net income of ≈$570M and a median base of ≈$2.10/share (−5.3%); the published scenario paths re-run on that base print IV@15% ≈$21.08 and weighted IRR ≈9.36% — still Tier D. The scored base stays the as-filed $2.2132 (the filed FY2025 diluted EPS): the segment-attributable figures an adjustment needs are 10-K note figures, not outputs of this run's dcf_numbers.json / ttm.json / financials_history.csv, so an adjusted pin would sit outside bound (c)'s permitted sources.

## OVERRIDE — capex (bounded worker authority, filing kind)
- **The gap:** the preliminary engine run exited 4 with `DATA_GAP:capex` — capex missing for FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 of the last 3 under every candidate tag (statements.json: no capital-expenditure figure filed for 45 periods with operating cash flow, 2015-06-30..2026-06-30). No tier was emitted, correctly.
- **The decision:** judgment.json carries `capex_override = {value: 147000000, kind: "filing", source: "Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-26), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows (pp. 107-108), investing activities line 'Additions to property and equipment and capitalized software': $(147) million for FY2025, with $(146) million for FY2024 and $(132) million for FY2023 in the same statement"}` with an ack_reason recording that the value is out-of-band by construction (no filed capex value exists under any candidate tag in the last 3 FY to band against — the last tagged fact ttm.py can find is FY2014). The statement was verified to reconcile exactly with this line in all three years (FY2025: operating $5,828M + investing -$8,934M + financing $2,263M = the reported net change in cash of -$843M).
- **Known imperfection, stated:** the single $147M value fills every missing period (key_numbers.md: periods filled 2016-12-31 through 2025-12-31) — it overstates FY2024 capex by $1M (true $146M) and FY2023 by $15M (true $132M). Immaterial either way: the scored base is the NI-based base_override (net income already carries the depreciation charge), and ~$140M/yr of capex is ~2.5% of the rejected OCF base.

## BASE OVERRIDE — measured impact
- **Measured impact (key_numbers.md, measured by make_score.py on the base actually used, same final configuration with overrides toggled off):** base OE/share $19.60 (no override) → $2.21 (with override), −88.71%; weighted IRR 58.70% → 9.73% (−48.97pp). Unblocks tier: YES — without the judgment overrides the filing gap blocks scoring entirely, and without the base_override the score is the OCF artifact below.

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate/narrow; scale leadership, no structural pricing power
Justification: the largest U.S. title insurer with scale, agency/direct distribution, title-plant data and industry-leading adjusted pre-tax title margins (15.9% FY2025, 17.8% in Q2 2026), plus F&G diversifying earnings away from housing — against a commodity, rate-filed product, earnings hostage to housing volumes and F&G marks, and a return record that does not support a wide moat. Return evidence as required: fundamentals.json carries no roic_proxy and no gross margin for an insurer presentation (both null), so the evidence is ROE — GAAP ROE was 7.5% in FY2023, 16.4% in FY2024 and 8.1% in FY2025 (fundamentals.json), after 21.2% in FY2022 and 29.7% in FY2021 in the title boom: volatile, and mostly below a wide-moat level through the recent cycle.
- FOR:
  - Largest U.S. title insurer — scale in direct and agency distribution, title plants/data and claims infrastructure rivals cannot replicate cheaply
  - Industry-leading adjusted pre-tax title margin: 15.9% for FY2025 and 17.8% in Q2 2026 (15.7% H1 2026), with commercial direct revenue +24% YoY in H1 2026
  - F&G second engine: AUM before flow reinsurance $73.1B at FY2025 (+12% YoY) and $74.7B at Q2 2026; F&G contributed 30% of FY2025 adjusted net earnings, diversifying away from housing volumes
  - Capital return at scale: ~$800M returned in FY2025 ($546M dividends + $251M buybacks); DPS $2.02 in FY2025, 4 consecutive growth years, no cut since 2011 (fundamentals.json)
  - Technology/operating leverage in title: inHere platform engaging ~80% of residential sale transactions (Q2 2026), disciplined expense management through a weak housing cycle
- AGAINST:
  - Commodity, rate-regulated product — title premiums are filed/regulated and re-shopped deal by deal; no structural pricing power, agent commissions were $2,518M in FY2025 against $5,824M of direct+agency premiums
  - Housing/mortgage hostage: title volumes track purchase/refinance transactions, which remain at historically low levels; a prolonged housing freeze compresses the core engine
  - F&G earnings are mark- and assumption-driven: GAAP net earnings swung $2,797M (FY2021) to $517M (FY2023) to $1,270M (FY2024) to $602M (FY2025) on recognized gains/losses, market-risk-benefit and reserve changes; credit impairments in the $73B investment portfolio are the tail
  - Returns do not prove a wide moat: GAAP ROE 7.5% / 16.4% / 8.1% in FY2023/24/25 (fundamentals.json), no roic_proxy filed for an insurer presentation
  - Corporate drag and complexity: Corporate & Other lost $458M attributable in FY2025 including the F&G distribution deferred-tax adjustment ($471M); the Dec 31, 2025 ~12% F&G share distribution cut FNF's stake and its share of F&G earnings
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — v5 final run (2026-10-19)
Growth recalibration (written reason): the engine's g_base of −1.73% is not usable as printed for this insurer. Its revenue series is the contract-revenue tag, which for FNF is only a slice of the business — the CSV revenue line is $2,099,000,000 for FY2025 against filer-total revenue of $14,445,000,000 in fundamentals.json — so the blend's revenue CAGRs (5y −2.64%, 3y −2.03%, latest YoY +9.10%, key_numbers.md) describe that slice, not the company, and the OE/share CAGR component (−5.73%) is measured on the rejected OCF definition. Scenario starts were therefore set against the NI base actually used, via offsets (−0.102735 / −0.022735 / +0.077265 / +0.137265 / +0.217265 vs g_base) to −12 / −4 / **+6** / +12 / +20% (the engine floored the super-bear start at −10.0% as printed in key_numbers.md). Sanity check against prints: total revenue grew +5.6% in FY2025 and TTM revenue +13.0% YoY (fundamentals.json); Q2 2026 revenue was $4,051M vs $3,635M a year earlier, adjusted net EPS grew to $1.39 from $1.16 in Q2 and to $2.31 from $1.95 in H1 2026. The base start of +6% sits at the FY2025 revenue print and well below the TTM revenue and adjusted-EPS prints — it carries normalization of the one-off $471M tax charge in the base year, not momentum; the bull start of +12% sits at the TTM revenue print; only the super-bull start (+20%) exceeds the prints, with this written reason: it is the housing-recovery case (title volumes are at historic lows, so a recovery plus F&G AUM compounding is the one path that outruns current prints), and it carries only 10% probability. The bears are lived experience, not stress fantasy: GAAP net earnings fell from $2,797M in FY2021 to $517M in FY2023 the last time housing froze and F&G marks turned. Probabilities 10/25/30/25/10; OE multipliers 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25. Price $39.62.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | -10.0% | 0.75 | Housing freeze deepens and F&G credit/mark losses land together; earnings retrace toward the FY2023 print | $8.06 | 4.66% |
| Bear | 25% | -4.0% | 0.90 | Housing stays frozen, F&G spreads compress; earnings grind down from the depressed base | $12.45 | 6.18% |
| Base | 30% | 6.0% | 1.00 | Tax-charge normalization plus mid-single-digit revenue growth (commercial title, F&G AUM), fading over the CAP | $20.99 | 9.25% |
| Bull | 25% | 12.0% | 1.10 | TTM revenue pace holds; title margin stays at the Q2 2026 level and housing begins to recover | $29.56 | 12.05% |
| Super bull | 10% | 20.0% | 1.25 | Full housing recovery off historic-low volumes plus F&G compounding at print rates | $46.50 | 16.83% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $22.26 (−43.8% vs price), IV@12% $29.74, IV@10% $38.11, weighted IRR 9.73%, base-case IRR 9.25%**
- **Tier by numbers: D.** Diagnostics (key_numbers.md): OE yield 5.59%, terminal value 19.3% of IV@15%, scenario spread 5.77x, net debt 2.93x normalized OE, 9.6 months since FY end. IRR band: bear 6.18% (tier D) → bull 12.05% (tier C). Hurdle-clearing prices (weighted path): 15% at $22.26, 20% at $15.56, 25% at $11.89.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **DATA_GAP:capex** (preliminary run): resolved by the filing override — see OVERRIDE (capex). The gap, the decision, the single-value imperfection and the measured impact are all recorded in fields (judgment.json, dcf_numbers.json overrides_applied/override_impact, overrides_registry.json), not just here.
- **STALE_FY** (FY ended 9.6 months ago): resolved by the TTM check — ttm.py was run through Q2 2026 and its legs are quoted in the Owner's earnings section. The base was pinned by base_override to the NI median, which the TTM evidence corroborates directionally (TTM net income $772,000,000 in fundamentals.json, above FY2025's $602,000,000 — the recovery is in the run-rate and is carried in the scenario starts rather than in a TTM OCF base that measures the wrong quantity; ttm.py's own capex leg is a 2014/2015 period-mismatch artifact, stated there).
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2023, 2024, 2025): resolved — the gap is structural insurer plumbing, not a one-off to excuse: annuity deposits and future-policy-benefit builds run through OCF while $23,198M of FY2025 investment purchases sit in investing. The one genuine one-off inside net income runs the other way: FY2025 GAAP NI is *depressed* by the $471M noncash deferred-tax charge on the F&G distribution. The divergence is the reason the base is net income, not OCF (see BASE OVERRIDE).
- **SHARES_FALLBACK** (no diluted count filed for 2017): noted — 2017 history uses the dei outstanding count (274,438,819, shares_tag in financials_history.csv); per-share history there is approximate. No median year (2023–2025) is affected: all three carry filed diluted counts.
- **SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH** (Finance): accepted in full. An insurer's distributable earnings are bounded by regulatory capital, its claim/benefit provisions are a through-cycle cost OCF only pretends to carry, and its real asset deployment is an investing flow. Confidence is low, the base was replaced with the sector's honest proxy, and the tier is soft — see the method range, which is the honest headline for this name.
- **OVERRIDE_APPLIED:capex**: see OVERRIDE (capex).
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (5.77x): real — a housing-cyclical title engine bolted to a mark-sensitive annuity book IS this wide (super-bear IV@15% $8.06 vs super-bull $46.50). Confidence is low (also mandated by the sector flag), and the verdict is sized to the conservative end (TIER_BAND).
- **TIER_BAND** (bear tier D at 6.18% vs bull tier C at 12.05%): accepted — the verdict spans tiers because the housing cycle does. Any position sizing belongs at the bear end.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The honest headline is the method range, and here it is extreme. The same final scenario set on the engine's native OCF bases prints **Tier S**: weighted IRR 58.70% on the TTM OCF base (key_numbers.md measured impact, overrides off) and 68.24% with IV@15% $232.69 on the normalized OCF base in the capex-only run — a fake S, produced entirely by counting annuity deposits and policy-benefit builds as earnings while their investment deployment sits in investing. On the scored GAAP-NI median base the company prints **Tier D, weighted IRR 9.73%, IV@15% $22.26**. On the company's own adjusted-earnings base — FY2025 adjusted net earnings of $1,352M, $4.97/share (FY2025 earnings release; FY2024: $4.63) — the identical scenario set prints **Tier B, weighted IRR 18.04%, IV@15% $49.98** (bear 11.09% → bull 22.44%), measured in a separate engine run of this same configuration. Anyone quoting one number for FNF without its method is hiding the ball; the two defensible earnings bases span D to B, and the scored verdict sits at the conservative end of that range, per the sizing rule.
- Why the scored end is the GAAP end: the adjusted base strips every F&G mark and recognized loss as if they were free — for an annuity writer holding a $73B investment portfolio, marks and credit are a recurring cost of the business, not noise. But the GAAP base is not clean either: its median year carries the $471M one-off distribution tax charge, which is why the base-case growth start (+6%) carries normalization and why the range, not the point, is the finding.
- The cross-checks the model cannot do sit between the ends: at $39.62 the market pays 8.0x FY2025 adjusted EPS of $4.97 and a $2.02 dividend (fundamentals.json DPS) — pricing in roughly the adjusted run-rate with little housing recovery, which is closer to the B-end economics than to D. What the D is really saying is narrower: on *GAAP* earnings as filed, with F&G marks charged in full, $39.62 does not clear a 15% hurdle; it clears 15% only below $22.26 on that base ($49.98 on the adjusted base).
- What would change the verdict: a housing recovery (title is the operating leverage — purchase orders are at historic lows, so volume normalization is the super-bull path), F&G credit losses landing (the bear path), or further F&G distributions/sales shrinking FNF's share of the steadier earnings stream (the Dec 2025 distribution already cut the stake to ~70% and triggered the tax charge).

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (weighted IRR 9.73% on the v5 final inputs; tier by numbers D, no override of the tier — the judgment sits in the base, where the sector defect is; method range D to B across defensible earnings bases, S on the rejected OCF artifact)
- Confidence: **Low** (sector-model mismatch, a 5.77x scenario spread, and a D→C tier band; the filing data itself is solid once the capex gap override is in)
- One-liner: Largest U.S. title insurer plus F&G annuities, moat 5/10 — on the only honest base for an insurer (median GAAP net income $2.21/sh, not the $23.14/sh OCF artifact) the weighted IRR is 9.73% (IV@15% $22.26 vs $39.62), so it clears 15% only below ~$22; the GAAP base carries a $471M one-off deferred-tax charge — on the company's $4.97 FY2025 adjusted EPS the same scenarios print Tier B (18.04%), so the method range is D to B; insurer-model mismatch, confidence low.
